Flying-fish print forms

Parametric props drawn from the exported STL triangles, in two sets. Morphology set: three body plans at 0.1 kg (v2, corrected body profile); 1 m = 350 mm. Wing-geometry comparison set: Cypselurus at 0.05 kg (dx-nca controlled run) (v2, corrected body profile); 1 m = 450 mm. Biological values are in SI; fins are thickened print plates. Printer and resin are not chosen yet, and nothing has been sliced or printed.

Form studies pending a validated candidate. Engineered illustrative form. Not an ancestor, not a viable organism, not a demonstrated evolutionary path, not flight-tested. Fins are thickened for printing.
drag to rotate · wheel or pinch to zoom

Biological design point and the prop made from it

Wing area follows Fish 1990's definition (pectoral + pelvic fins + body rectangles at the fin bases). Wing loading is m·g/S. The solver is dx-guilds' z3 model at commit 948c2e1 (blob sha256 de0acf47ffc7ffbe…); "feasible" means an exact point satisfies the declared constraints in that model, nothing more.

Analogues and engineered forms

Sourced relationships are solid; conjectured routes between the engineered forms are dashed red and claim nothing about reachability.

Not checked

  • Global self-intersection, slicing, supports, cups and minima. These depend on printer, resin and orientation, and PreForm checks them.
  • No physical print and no PreForm run. Resin volume and print time come only from the slicer.
  • Aerodynamics of the prop. Visual likeness is not aerodynamic fidelity. A–C have no glide simulation; N1–N3 carry dx-nca's point-mass simulation with assumed polars, which compares S and AR and calibrates nothing.
  • Wall thickness is checked against 1 mm (our provisional prop choice) on sampled faces only.
  • Biological feasibility, ancestry and evolutionary reachability. None are claimed.
